stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview is complex — requires requirement elaboration (state sync, rendering fidelity, concurrent edits) followed by testability and security hardening. Both agents assigned; openspec first, then speckit reviews.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability: Live Preview mode for Contentstack CMS. No preview pathway exists in current code — useContent and ContentstackContext only fetch published content. Attachment points are useContent (236 callers) and ContentstackContext (provider). VCs derived from description since ACs are empty; each VC names a specific user-facing surface and a concrete observable check. Contentstack.io is unreachable at test time, so VCs state the mock assumption explicitly.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with useful context about the novel capability and attachment points. I created all 12 ACs from scratch based on the story title, description, and file paths. Key design decisions: (1) AC-3 specifies a 5-second SLA for real-time updates — this is a placeholder that should be validated against Contentstack's actual Live Preview SDK latency characteristics. (2) AC-6 gates preview behind environment detection — this is a security assumption; the actual gating mechanism (build-time flag, environment variable, auth check) is implementation detail, but the observable outcome (preview not activatable in production) is what matters. (3) AC-9 covers invalid/expired token handling. (4) AC-10 addresses cross-contamination risk when multiple entries are previewed. (5) AC-12 covers the edge case of null/empty draft fields. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I did not have access to the contents of useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, or ContentstackLink.tsx. The criteria are derived from the story title, description, and file names alone. Once file contents are available, criteria may need refinement — for example, contentCard.ts may define specific fields that AC-8 should enumerate, and ContentstackContext.tsx may already have partial preview infrastructure that changes the scope.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed, but value distribution was lopsided. OpenSpec identified attachment points (useContent, ContentstackContext) and noted the novel capability, but produced no concrete acceptance criteria (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0). Speckit then created all 12 ACs from scratch — effectively performing both requirement elaboration and its own review role, resulting in significant role overlap. Speckit's ACs are thoughtful (SLA gating, token handling, cross-contamination, null fields), but it explicitly lacked access to useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, and ContentstackLink.tsx, meaning criteria were derived from titles and descriptions alone and may not reflect actual field structures or existing partial infrastructure. The 5-second SLA in AC-3 is acknowledged as a placeholder requiring validation. Human review should verify ACs against actual source files and confirm or adjust the SLA.
